# Use Cases

## Supported

| ID | Use case | Actor | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| UC-1 | Interactive coding assistance in the terminal | Developer | The developer runs `opencode` (full TUI) or `opencode mini` (minimal UI) from `packages/cli`, picks `build` or `plan` agents, and iterates with the session runtime in `packages/core/src/session`. |
| UC-2 | Coding assistance in web and desktop apps | Developer | The developer uses the `packages/app` web UI (`opencode serve`, `opencode pair`) or the `packages/desktop` Electron app, sharing session timeline components from `packages/session-ui`. |
| UC-3 | Non-interactive headless runs | Developer, Operator | The operator runs `opencode run "<msg>"` with `--model`, `--agent`, `--format`, `--session`, and `--continue` flags, or drives `opencode api` against the OpenAPI server for scripting. |
| UC-4 | Multi-provider model choice | Developer | The developer lists models with `opencode models`, manages credentials with `opencode auth login/logout/list`, and relies on `packages/ai` provider clients plus the models.dev catalog in `packages/core/src/models-dev`. |
| UC-5 | Durable sessions with inbox admission | Developer | The developer creates, resumes, forks, archives, and searches sessions (`session` and `message` API groups in `packages/protocol/src/groups`), backed by `session_v2`, `session_inbox`, and `session_message` tables. |
| UC-6 | Snapshots, sharing, and sync | Developer | The developer snapshots session state, shares via URL, and syncs through the `SyncServer` Durable Object in `packages/function/src/api.ts`. |
| UC-7 | Tool use with permissions | Developer | The model calls Location-scoped tools from `packages/core/src` (file, shell, search, web) while the developer gates side effects with permission flags and the `permission` API group. |
| UC-8 | Skills and commands | Developer | The developer extends agent behavior with skills and slash commands (`skill` and `command` API groups, `packages/core/src/skill*` and `command.ts`). |
| UC-9 | Plugins and MCP servers | Plugin author | The author ships plugins via the `@opencode/plugin` SDK (`packages/plugin`) with namespaced hooks, and connects external context through MCP servers (`mcp` and `plugin` API groups). |
| UC-10 | Programmatic embedding via SDK | Developer | The developer embeds the agent with the `@opencode/sdk` in-process host (`OpenCode.create()`) or the generated `@opencode/client` typed HTTP client. |
| UC-11 | Agent interop over ACP | Developer | External editors drive OpenCode through the Agent Client Protocol server (`opencode acp` in `packages/cli/src/acp`). |
| UC-12 | CI assistance via GitHub Action | Operator | The operator runs OpenCode in pipelines with `github/action.yml`, triaging issues and reviewing PRs from `/opencode` or `/oc` comments. |
| UC-13 | Self-hosted headless service | Operator | The operator serves the Hono plus Effect HttpApi (`packages/server`, OpenAPI at `/openapi.json`) with `opencode serve` and manages it via `opencode service start/stop/restart/status`. |
| UC-14 | Enterprise team hosting | Operator | The operator deploys the console, enterprise teams app, stats, identity, and file services (`packages/console`, `packages/enterprise`, `packages/stats`, `services/*`) through `sst.config.ts` and `infra/`. |
| UC-15 | Project and workspace management | Developer | The developer registers projects, directories, worktrees, and VCS info (`project`, `worktree`, `vcs` API groups) backed by the `project`, `project_directory`, and `worktree` tables. |
| UC-16 | Documentation and changelog sites | Contributor | Contributors read and extend the docs site (`services/www`, `src/docs`), the posts site (`packages/posts`), and the changelog worker (`services/changelog`). |

## Wanted

| ID | Use case | Actor | Description | Signal |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| UC-17 | Chat and notifications inside Slack | Developer | Developers want to drive sessions from Slack, but no Slack bot package exists in the repo today. | FEAT-0012 (stale, under review) |

## Out of scope

- Training or fine-tuning models (OpenCode consumes existing providers).
- Hosting or managing the user's code repositories (OpenCode operates on local directories only).
- General-purpose chat outside a coding or project context.
